title: Genesis Chapter 43 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Genesis chapter 43 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Genesis Chapter 43 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Genesis Chapter 43.

questions.question: What was sore in the land according to Genesis 43?
questions.correctAnswer: The famine
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:1 states, 'And the famine was sore in the land.'

questions.question: Why did their father tell them to go buy food again?
options: Because they had eaten up the corn they brought from Egypt
Because they wanted to bring gifts
questions.correctAnswer: Because they had eaten up the corn they brought from Egypt
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:2 says they had eaten up the corn brought from Egypt, so their father said to buy more food.

questions.question: What condition did the man set for them to see his face again?
options: Their brother must be with them
They must not bring their brother
questions.correctAnswer: Their brother must be with them
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:3 states the man said, 'Ye shall not see my face, except your brother be with you.'

questions.question: What did Judah say they would do if their brother went with them?
options: They would go down and buy food
They would send their brother alone
They would ask for more money
questions.correctAnswer: They would go down and buy food
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:4 says, 'If thou wilt send our brother with us, we will go down and buy thee food.'

questions.question: What was Israel's reaction when he learned they told the man about their brother?
options: He asked why they dealt ill with him
questions.correctAnswer: He asked why they dealt ill with him
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:6 says Israel asked, 'Wherefore dealt ye so ill with me, as to tell the man whether ye had yet a brother?'

questions.question: What reason did the brothers give for telling the man about their brother?
options: The man asked strictly about their state and kindred
They wanted to trick the man
questions.correctAnswer: The man asked strictly about their state and kindred
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:7 says, 'The man asked us straitly... and we told him according to the tenor of these words.'

questions.question: What did Judah offer to do for his brother before going to Egypt?
options: Be surety for him and bear the blame if he failed
questions.correctAnswer: Be surety for him and bear the blame if he failed
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:9 says Judah will be surety and bear the blame if he does not bring the brother back.

questions.question: What did Israel instruct his sons to take to the man as a present?
options: Best fruits, balm, honey, spices, myrrh, nuts, and almonds
questions.correctAnswer: Best fruits, balm, honey, spices, myrrh, nuts, and almonds
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:11 lists these items as the present Israel told them to carry.

questions.question: What unusual instruction did Israel give about the money?
options: Take double money and carry the money found in their sacks again
Give the money to the man
questions.correctAnswer: Take double money and carry the money found in their sacks again
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:12 tells them to take double money and the money found in their sacks again.

questions.question: True or False: Judah said they would not go down to buy food unless their brother went with them.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:5 states, 'But if thou wilt not send him, we will not go down.'

questions.question: True or False: Israel was willing to send Benjamin with his sons to Egypt after Judah's request.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:13 says Israel told them to take their brother and go again to the man.

questions.question: True or False: The brothers were confident they would not be accused because the money was returned in their sacks.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:18 shows the men were afraid they might be accused because of the money found in their sacks.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph was moved to weep when he saw his brother Benjamin.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:30 says Joseph's bowels yearned upon his brother and he wept in his chamber.

questions.question: In Genesis 43, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Take double money in your hand
Carry a present of fruits and spices
Buy food again because corn was finished
questions.correctAnswer: Buy food again because corn was finished
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:2 shows the father told them to buy food after they had eaten up the corn they brought from Egypt, which is the earliest instruction among these.

questions.question: What did Joseph command when he saw Benjamin with the men?
options: Bring these men home and prepare a meal
questions.correctAnswer: Bring these men home and prepare a meal
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:16 says Joseph told his steward to bring the men home and make ready because they would dine with him at noon.

medium.title: Genesis Chapter 43 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Genesis Chapter 43 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Genesis 43:13, what did Israel's sons take with them when they went to see Joseph again?
questions.correctAnswer: Their brother Benjamin
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:13 instructs them to 'Take also your brother, and arise, go again unto the man,' showing that they were to bring Benjamin along with them. This follows the previous verses where their father Israel agrees to send Benjamin to ensure they meet Joseph (Genesis 43:11-14).

questions.question: What did Israel ask God to grant his sons before meeting Joseph in Genesis 43:14?
questions.correctAnswer: Mercy
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:14 says, 'And God Almighty give you mercy before the man,' indicating Israel's prayer for mercy so that Joseph would send away their other brother and Benjamin, reflecting his deep concern and faith in God's providence (Genesis 43:13-15).

questions.question: What did the men carry in their hands when they went down to Egypt to stand before Joseph as stated in Genesis 43:15?
questions.correctAnswer: Double money and Benjamin
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:15 states, 'And the men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and rose up, and went down to Egypt,' showing their obedience to Israel's instructions and their faith in God's guidance (Genesis 43:11-13).

questions.question: How did Joseph respond when he saw Benjamin with his brothers in Genesis 43:16?
options: He ordered the men to be imprisoned
He commanded the men to be brought home and prepared a meal
He sent them away without food
questions.correctAnswer: He commanded the men to be brought home and prepared a meal
questions.explanation: In Genesis 43:16, Joseph tells the ruler of his house to bring the men home and prepare a meal for them, showing his favor and concern, especially upon seeing Benjamin (Genesis 43:15-17).

questions.question: Why were the men afraid when brought into Joseph’s house according to Genesis 43:18?
options: They feared Joseph’s wrath over their money
They feared a wild animal attack
They were afraid of the food
questions.correctAnswer: They feared Joseph’s wrath over their money
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:18 explains the men’s fear because 'the money that was returned in our sacks at the first time' might cause Joseph to accuse them and enslave them, highlighting their anxiety and mistrust despite their innocence (Genesis 43:21-23).

questions.question: What did the men say to the steward at Joseph's house in Genesis 43:20 to explain their first visit?
options: We came to spy on Egypt
We came to deliver a message
questions.correctAnswer: We came to buy food
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:20 records the men telling the steward, 'O sir, we came indeed down at the first time to buy food,' showing their honest intent and concern over the misunderstanding about the money in their sacks (Genesis 43:18-22).

questions.question: How does Genesis 43:23 teach about God’s providence and reassurance in times of fear?
questions.correctAnswer: God gives treasure and peace
questions.explanation: In Genesis 43:23 the steward says, 'Peace be to you, fear not: your God...hath given you treasure in your sacks,' reassuring the brothers that God is in control and providing for them even in difficult situations, linking faith and peace (Genesis 43:18-22).

questions.question: What practical lesson about hospitality and care can be learned from Genesis 43:24?
options: Hospitality includes cleaning and feeding animals
questions.correctAnswer: Hospitality includes cleaning and feeding animals
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:24 shows the steward giving water for washing feet and feeding the asses, teaching that true hospitality involves caring for both guests and their animals, reflecting kindness and respect (Genesis 43:17-24).

questions.question: What does Genesis 43:14 imply about the importance of praying for others and trusting God in difficult family circumstances?
options: Prayer is unnecessary in family matters
God should be trusted to show mercy
questions.correctAnswer: God should be trusted to show mercy
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:14 shows Israel’s prayer for mercy on his sons before meeting Joseph, teaching the importance of entrusting family concerns to God’s mercy and care, encouraging faith amid uncertainty (Genesis 43:13-15).

questions.question: How does the exchange between the brothers and the steward in Genesis 43:21-22 illustrate honesty and integrity?
options: They admitted the money in their sacks was unknown to them
They tried to steal more money
questions.correctAnswer: They admitted the money in their sacks was unknown to them
questions.explanation: Verses 21-22 show the brothers openly stating they found money in their sacks and brought more money to buy food, demonstrating integrity and honesty despite their fear of suspicion (Genesis 43:18-23).

questions.question: What can Christians learn about faith and obedience from Israel’s decision in Genesis 43:13 to send Benjamin with his sons?
questions.correctAnswer: Faith requires risk and obedience
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:13 shows Israel obeying despite his fear of losing Benjamin, teaching that faith often involves stepping out in obedience even when the outcome is uncertain, relying on God’s protection (Genesis 43:11-14).

questions.question: True or False: According to Genesis 43:16, Joseph planned a private meal with only his Egyptian servants, excluding his brothers.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:16 says Joseph ordered to bring the men into his house and prepare a meal for them to dine with him, showing he planned to include his brothers, not exclude them.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 43:18 reveals the brothers’ fear that Joseph might make them bondmen because of the money found in their sacks.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:18 clearly states the men were afraid they were brought in because of the money returned in their sacks and feared becoming bondmen, reflecting their mistrust despite their innocence.

questions.question: True or False: Genesis 43:24 describes the steward refusing to provide water for washing the brothers’ feet.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:24 states the steward brought the men into Joseph’s house, gave them water to wash their feet, and provided food for their asses, showing hospitality and care rather than refusal.

questions.question: What does Genesis 43:23 teach about the relationship between God and the circumstances of Joseph’s brothers?
options: God punishes them for their sins
God has provided for them and orchestrated events
God is angry with their family
questions.correctAnswer: God has provided for them and orchestrated events
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:23 says the steward reassured the brothers that their God and their father's God gave them treasure in their sacks, indicating God's providence and care even in difficult times (Genesis 43:18-22).

hard.title: Genesis Chapter 43 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Genesis Chapter 43.

questions.question: What did Joseph do immediately after seeing his brother Benjamin in Genesis 43?
options: He questioned them about their father
questions.correctAnswer: He wept in his chamber
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:30 states Joseph made haste because his bowels yearned upon his brother; he sought where to weep and entered into his chamber to weep.

questions.question: What reason is given in Genesis 43 for Egyptians not eating bread with Hebrews?
options: Because it was an abomination to the Egyptians
They did not speak the same language
questions.correctAnswer: Because it was an abomination to the Egyptians
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:32 explains that Egyptians would not eat bread with Hebrews because that was an abomination unto the Egyptians.

questions.question: Which brother's portion was five times as much as the others at the meal with Joseph?
questions.correctAnswer: Benjamin
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:34 states that Benjamin's mess was five times as much as any of the others' at the meal.

questions.question: What did Joseph's brothers bring to him as a present when they came to Egypt the second time?
options: A little balm, honey, spices, myrrh, nuts, and almonds
questions.correctAnswer: A little balm, honey, spices, myrrh, nuts, and almonds
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:11 lists the present Israel instructed his sons to bring: balm, honey, spices, myrrh, nuts, and almonds.

questions.question: What was Judah's role in assuring Israel about bringing Benjamin to Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: He became surety for Benjamin
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:9 shows Judah said he would be surety for Benjamin and take the blame if he did not return him.

questions.question: What was the significance of the double money the brothers carried the second time to Egypt?
options: To compensate for previous money found in their sacks
questions.correctAnswer: To compensate for previous money found in their sacks
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:12 instructs them to carry double money, including the money returned in their sacks, possibly to correct an oversight.

questions.question: Who was brought out to the brothers by Joseph's steward at the house in Egypt?
questions.correctAnswer: Simeon
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:23 records that the steward brought Simeon out to the brothers.

questions.question: How did Joseph address the men when they bowed before him and brought the present?
options: He asked about their welfare and their father
questions.correctAnswer: He asked about their welfare and their father
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:27 states Joseph asked, 'Is your father well, the old man of whom ye spake? Is he yet alive?'

questions.question: What was Joseph's emotional reaction to seeing Benjamin, according to the chapter's original Hebrew expression?
options: His bowels yearned upon his brother
questions.correctAnswer: His bowels yearned upon his brother
questions.explanation: The phrase 'bowels did yearn' in Genesis 43:30 comes from Hebrew 'raḥam' which expresses deep compassion and tender affection.

questions.question: What literary device is evident in the arrangement of Genesis 43, especially in the interactions between Joseph and his brothers?
questions.correctAnswer: Chiasmus
questions.explanation: Genesis 43 shows chiastic structure with mirrored events: the brothers’ journey, their presentation before Joseph, and the revelation of family ties, a common Hebrew literary device.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of reconciliation depicted in Genesis 43?
questions.correctAnswer: 2 Corinthians 5:18-19
questions.explanation: 2 Corinthians 5:18-19 speaks of the ministry of reconciliation, echoing the reconciliation between Joseph and his brothers in Genesis 43.

questions.question: According to Genesis 43, what cultural practice explains why the Egyptians ate separately from the Hebrews?
questions.correctAnswer: Religious abomination of sharing bread
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:32 explains Egyptians considered it an abomination to eat bread with Hebrews, reflecting cultural and religious separation.

questions.question: How does Genesis 43 foreshadow the later reunion and forgiveness themes found in the story of Joseph?
options: By showing the brothers' fear of Joseph's anger
By depicting Joseph's emotional response and special treatment of Benjamin
questions.correctAnswer: By depicting Joseph's emotional response and special treatment of Benjamin
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:30-34 show Joseph's yearning for Benjamin and his generous giving, foreshadowing reconciliation and forgiveness.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph accused his brothers of stealing money when they returned to buy food the second time.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:23 shows the steward assured the brothers their God gave them the treasure; Joseph did not accuse them.

questions.question: True or False: Joseph's sending of larger portions to Benjamin can be seen as a sign of his special favor towards him.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:34 states Benjamin's mess was five times as much as any of the others, indicating special favor.

theological.title: Genesis Chapter 43 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Genesis Chapter 43 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Genesis 43:3-5 reveal about Judah's understanding of the conditions set by the Egyptian man regarding their brother?
options: They must bring their brother to see the man or they will not be allowed to buy food.
They can buy food without bringing their brother if they pay double.
The man wants only one brother to come with them to buy food.
They should leave their brother at home and return with food only.
questions.correctAnswer: They must bring their brother to see the man or they will not be allowed to buy food.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:3-5 shows Judah stating that the man solemnly declared they would not see his face unless their brother was with them, indicating the requirement to bring their brother to buy food.

questions.question: What theological doctrine is illustrated by Judah's willingness to personally guarantee Benjamin's safety in Genesis 43:8-9?
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of substitutionary suretyship
questions.explanation: In Genesis 43:8-9, Judah offers himself as surety for Benjamin, bearing personal responsibility for his return, which illustrates substitutionary suretyship, a concept where one person guarantees another's safety or debt.

questions.question: How does Genesis 43:14 reflect Israel's faith and fear regarding the fate of his children?
options: It shows a prayer for mercy and an expression of readiness to accept bereavement if it occurs.
It expresses confidence that God will protect all his children without exception.
It reveals Israel's disbelief in God's providence over his family.
It indicates Israel's plan to send all his sons to Egypt without worry.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows a prayer for mercy and an expression of readiness to accept bereavement if it occurs.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:14 records Israel praying for God's mercy to secure Benjamin's safe return, while also expressing his sorrowful acceptance if he loses his children, showing both faith and fear.

questions.question: What divine attribute is demonstrated in Genesis 43:23 when the steward reassures the brothers about their money found in their sacks?
questions.correctAnswer: God's providence
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:23 states that the steward said their God had given them treasure in their sacks, demonstrating God's providence in providing and protecting their resources.

questions.question: What does Joseph's emotional response in Genesis 43:30 reveal about his human nature and foreshadows Christ's compassionate heart?
options: Joseph's deep love and compassion for his brother, indicating a human empathy that foreshadows Christ's heart.
Joseph's anger and desire for revenge against his brothers.
Joseph's disbelief in his brother's survival.
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph's deep love and compassion for his brother, indicating a human empathy that foreshadows Christ's heart.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:30 shows Joseph's bowels yearning upon seeing Benjamin and his weeping in private, revealing his profound compassion, which typologically points to Christ’s empathetic and compassionate nature (Hebrews 4:15).

questions.question: How does Genesis 43:16-17 contribute to the narrative arc of Joseph's reconciliation with his brothers?
options: Joseph invites his brothers to dine with him, signaling a move toward restoration and reconciliation.
Joseph refuses to meet his brothers and orders them imprisoned.
Joseph sends them away without food.
Joseph demands immediate payment for food.
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph invites his brothers to dine with him, signaling a move toward restoration and reconciliation.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:16-17 records Joseph ordering his servants to prepare a meal for his brothers, demonstrating a significant step toward familial restoration and foreshadowing eventual reconciliation.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Genesis 43:11 and Genesis 43:25 provide about Israel's faith expressed through gifts and preparation?
options: They reveal Israel's belief in divine favor and the use of gifts as expressions of faith and hope for mercy.
They show Israel's distrust in God and reliance solely on material gifts.
They illustrate Israel's rejection of reconciliation with Egypt.
They demonstrate Israel's aim to bribe Joseph with wealth.
questions.correctAnswer: They reveal Israel's belief in divine favor and the use of gifts as expressions of faith and hope for mercy.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:11 commands taking the best fruits and gifts as a present, and verse 25 shows preparation for Joseph's arrival, together reflecting Israel’s faith and hope that these gifts would secure God's mercy through Joseph.

questions.question: What does Genesis 43:6-7 teach about human fallibility in communication and the consequences of incomplete disclosure?
options: It shows that incomplete disclosure about family status led to suspicion and tension with the Egyptian man.
It indicates that silence is the best policy in difficult negotiations.
It teaches that deception is justified to protect family interests.
It reveals that honesty always leads to immediate blessing.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that incomplete disclosure about family status led to suspicion and tension with the Egyptian man.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:6-7 recounts Israel’s displeasure at his sons for revealing the existence of their brother, which they did out of necessity, highlighting human imperfection in communication and its consequences.

questions.question: According to Genesis 43:32-33, what cultural or religious principle is illustrated by the separate seating arrangements during the meal?
options: The Egyptian abhorrence for eating bread with Hebrews, indicating cultural separation and purity laws.
The universal hospitality extended to strangers.
The unity of all peoples under one table.
The rejection of Egyptian customs by Joseph.
questions.correctAnswer: The Egyptian abhorrence for eating bread with Hebrews, indicating cultural separation and purity laws.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:32-33 explains that Egyptians did not eat bread with Hebrews as it was an abomination, illustrating cultural and religious separation between the two groups.

questions.question: What does Genesis 43:34 suggest about Joseph's attitude toward Benjamin compared to his other brothers, and what might this foreshadow?
options: Joseph gave Benjamin five times as much food, indicating special favor which may foreshadow Christ’s unique sonship.
Joseph ignored Benjamin completely during the meal.
Joseph gave all his brothers equal portions without distinction.
Joseph punished Benjamin by giving him less food.
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph gave Benjamin five times as much food, indicating special favor which may foreshadow Christ’s unique sonship.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:34 states Joseph sent messes to his brothers but gave Benjamin five times as much, highlighting Benjamin’s favored status and typologically pointing to Christ’s unique position as God's Son.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Genesis 43 teaches only human family drama with no divine involvement. What does Genesis 43:14-15 actually teach about God's role in the brothers' journey and Israel's hope?
options: It teaches that Israel invokes God Almighty’s mercy, indicating belief in divine providence over their circumstances.
It denies any divine role, focusing solely on human effort.
It teaches that God has abandoned Israel entirely.
It shows the brothers acting independently without God's involvement.
questions.correctAnswer: It teaches that Israel invokes God Almighty’s mercy, indicating belief in divine providence over their circumstances.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:14-15 records Israel praying that God Almighty grant mercy to his sons, showing active faith in God's sovereign care despite their dire situation, countering sceptical claims of divine absence.

questions.question: How do Genesis 43:1 and Genesis 43:2 together illustrate the human condition in relation to divine providence and necessity?
options: They show human dependence on God's provision during famine and the necessity to act by seeking sustenance.
They indicate that famine is a punishment with no hope of relief.
They suggest that humans can fully provide for themselves without God.
They teach that famine was a minor inconvenience easily resolved.
questions.correctAnswer: They show human dependence on God's provision during famine and the necessity to act by seeking sustenance.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:1 notes the severe famine, and 43:2 records Israel sending his sons to buy food, demonstrating human vulnerability and the need to depend on God's provision through practical means.

questions.question: What does the act of washing feet and providing provender for asses in Genesis 43:24 symbolize in the context of hospitality and covenantal relationship?
options: It symbolizes respectful hospitality and the maintenance of covenantal honor among God's people.
It indicates that the brothers were considered servants.
It shows a ritual cleansing required by Egyptian law.
It represents a rejection of the brothers by Joseph.
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes respectful hospitality and the maintenance of covenantal honor among God's people.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:24 describes the steward washing the brothers’ feet and feeding their asses, a customary sign of hospitality and respect, reflecting covenantal goodwill.

questions.question: What combined theological insight do Genesis 43:27-29 provide regarding Joseph's recognition of his family and God's grace?
options: Joseph's inquiry about their father and recognition of Benjamin reveals God’s grace restoring broken relationships.
Joseph shows suspicion and refuses to acknowledge his family.
Joseph ignores the mention of his mother’s son and focuses on wealth.
Joseph demands immediate punishment for his brothers.
questions.correctAnswer: Joseph's inquiry about their father and recognition of Benjamin reveals God’s grace restoring broken relationships.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:27-29 shows Joseph asking about his father and recognizing Benjamin as his brother, greeting him with grace, highlighting God’s work in healing family divisions.

questions.question: How does Genesis 43:18-22 teach the doctrine of divine sovereignty over human misunderstandings and fears?
options: It shows that although the brothers feared accusation, God's sovereignty ensured their money was returned, protecting them.
It indicates that human fears always lead to divine punishment.
It teaches that God ignores human affairs.
It reveals that the brothers were guilty and deserving of punishment.
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that although the brothers feared accusation, God's sovereignty ensured their money was returned, protecting them.
questions.explanation: Genesis 43:18-22 recounts the brothers’ fear of being accused of theft, but the steward reassures them that God provided for them by returning their money, illustrating divine sovereignty amid human fears.
